title: Accelerated Coordinate Descent for Directed Densest Subgraph Discovery

problem.claim: Find a subgraph of a directed graph with maximum density.

gap.claim: Existing directed densest subgraph solutions often provide weaker theoretical guarantees.

contributions.claim: A theoretically efficient (1+ε)-approximation algorithm for directed densest subgraph discovery.
A novel LP formulation and an efficient approximation algorithm based on accelerated random coordinate descent.
A theoretical iteration-efficiency comparison with state-of-the-art approximation algorithms.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly identify their LP formulation as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report an extensive empirical evaluation on 15 real large datasets.
The authors report that their algorithms are up to 1000× faster than the current state-of-the-art.
The authors report fewer iterations than state-of-the-art approximation algorithms for the same solution accuracy.

narrative_sequence.summary: Defines the directed densest subgraph problem and its application relevance.
Notes weaker theoretical guarantees in existing solutions.
Introduces a (1+ε)-approximation algorithm using a novel LP formulation and accelerated random coordinate descent.
Claims fewer iterations are required for the same solution accuracy.
Reports evaluation on 15 real large datasets and speedups up to 1000×.

source_observation.claim: The approach combines a problem-specific LP formulation with accelerated random coordinate descent.

interpretation.claim: Reformulating the optimization problem may enable more efficient iterative algorithms.

application.claim: When an optimization problem has weak existing guarantees, examine both its formulation and solver.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that this strategy generalizes beyond directed densest subgraph discovery.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the exact LP formulation.
The approximation and runtime conditions are not detailed.
The datasets, baselines, and experimental protocols are not identified.
The abstract does not provide independent verification of the reported speedups.
